title: num_ansi_colors ignores stream parameter
description:
Hello!

num_ansi_colours() stream parameter appears to be ignored, and the number of colours reported is always for stdout (for interactive sessions at least). For example, this seems wrong:

```
> crayon:::num_ansi_colors(file(tempfile()))
[1] 256
```

If I modify ``num_ansi_colors`` to report it's environment:

```
moo <- edit(crayon::num_ansi_colors)
# Insert "str(as.list(environment()))", before "if (is_stderr && sink.number("message") != 2)"
# https://github.com/r-lib/crayon/blob/main/R/aab-num-ansi-colors.R#L107
```

And run a few example cases:

```
moo()
moo(stdout())
moo("message")
moo("stderr")
moo(stderr())
moo(file(tempfile()))
```

Besides ``orig_stream`` all display the following output, and return 256, the number of colours for my stdout:

```
List of 10
 $ std         : chr "stdout"
 $ is_stdout   : logi TRUE
 $ is_stderr   : logi FALSE
 $ is_std      : logi TRUE
 $ orig_stream : 'file' int 3
  ..- attr(*, "conn_id")=<externalptr>
 $ cray_opt_num: NULL
 $ cray_opt_has: NULL
 $ env         : chr ""
 $ opt         : NULL
 $ stream      : 'terminal' int 1
```

I'm guessing the problem is in ``get_real_output``, which ignores the stream object it's handed, so the input parameter is never considered:

https://github.com/r-lib/crayon/blob/8b206a8d675d11f59492339fd6c798240c0bb17a/R/aac-num-ansi-colors.R#L6-L8

FWIW this doesn't seem to be an issue in ``cli``, is the version here considered deprecated? Or maybe there should be some syncing of code?

```
> cli:::num_ansi_colors(file(tempfile()))
[1] 1
```

For example:

```

text <- "你好"
```

```
[1] "\033[37m\033[37mä½ å¥½\033[37m\033[39m"
```

title: strip_style() returns garbled output in non-UTF-8 locale when UTF-8 characters are present
description:
If the colorized string contains UTF-8 characters, the resulting string from `strip_style()` is no longer of type "UTF-8" but of type "unknown". The reason for that is that `strip_style()` uses `gsub()` with parameter `useBytes=TRUE`. Manual for gsub states that:

```
     The main effect of ‘useBytes = TRUE’ is to avoid errors/warnings
     about invalid inputs and spurious matches in multibyte locales,
     but for ‘regexpr’ it changes the interpretation of the output.  It
     inhibits the conversion of inputs with marked encodings, and is
     forced if any input is found which is marked as ‘"bytes"’ (see
     ‘Encoding’).
``` 

If R is running under a locale which is non-UTF-8 (i.e. the value of l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]] is FALSE), this may lead to various "interesting" side effects.

**Demonstration**:

```
library(crayon)
foo <- paste0('\033[3m', '\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500', '\033[23m')
Encoding(foo)
Encoding(strip_style(foo))
```

The result is:

```
[1] "UTF-8"
[1] "unknown"
```

Now, consider this code:

```
nchar(foo)
nchar(strip_style(foo))
strip_style(foo)
```

The result depends on the locale:

under UTF-8 enabled locale (e.g. en_US.UTF-8), the results are:

```
[1] 17
[1] 8
[1] "────────"
```

Under another locale, e.g. en_US.ISO-8859-15, the results are

```
[1] 17
[1] 24
[1] "�\224\200�\224\200�\224\200�\224\200�\224\200�\224\200�\224\200�\224\200"
```

**What would be the expected output under ISO-8850-15**

```
[1] 17
[1] 8
[1] "<U+2500><U+2500><U+2500><U+2500><U+2500><U+2500><U+2500><U+2500>"
```

**Why is that important?**

CRAN uses a en_US.ISO-8859-15 locale in one of the platforms for checking. Any package that uses UTF-8 characters in combination with crayon may have unexpected and hard to track bugs when tested by CRAN. This very situation happened to me (package [colorDF](https://january3.github.io/colorDF/)) and the bug was infuriating to replicate and track.

title: Potential NAMESPACE/import issue?
description:
Hello,

I'm not sure why this issue seems to only affect me, but I am unable to install **crayon** from CRAN or github:

```
> install.packages('crayon')
trying URL 'https://mirror.las.iastate.edu/CRAN/src/contrib/crayon_1.5.0.tar.gz'
Content type 'application/x-gzip' length 40099 bytes (39 KB)
==================================================
downloaded 39 KB

* installing *source* package ‘crayon’ ...
```

The issue is that in the function `ansi_palettes()`, the call to `read.table()` doesn't explicitly specify the namespace. Again, no idea why this works for some and not others, but maybe you want to explicitly specify the namespace here, as it appears to affect installation on some R setups (and is probably better coding practice)?

title: Force all warnings to use crayon?
description:
Is there a way to force all warnings to use crayon styling? (obviously, you can do this with warnings you personally create, but what about warnings generated by other packages?)

The motivation here is that I often run scripts from a command line and want to be able to quickly scan through the output and have warnings/errors "pop" out. With errors, I can for example, add the following to .Rprofile:

```r
options(error = quote({cat(crayon::red$bold((geterrmessage())));
        if (!interactive()) q()}), show.error.messages=FALSE)
```

and it turns all the error messages bold red. But with warnings, there is no equivalent option (that I know of). Is there any way to force all warnings to appear, say, in bold magenta?

description:
It seems that when a job is lauched via `rstudioapi::jobRunScript()`, any resulting output is not colored by crayon despite it being permitted by the output environment:

```R

#red test works as expected:
jobID = rstudioapi::jobAdd('red')
rstudioapi::jobAddOutput(jobID,crayon::red('red'))

#green test doesn't:
tmp = tempfile()
write(
	'cat(crayon::green("green"))'
	, file = tmp
)
rstudioapi::jobRunScript(tmp,name='green')

#blue test does:
tmp = tempfile()
write(
	'cat("\u001b[34m blue")'
	, file = tmp
)
rstudioapi::jobRunScript(tmp,name='blue')
```

title: Error in clienv$num_colors[[std]] : subscript out of bounds
description:
In any of my terminals (iTerm with or without tmux, Terminal on Mac), when I executed 

```
> crayon::num_colors(TRUE)
```

I got the error message

```
Error in clienv$num_colors[[std]] : subscript out of bounds
```

This also prevented me from loading tidyverse in my terminal, which was a major problem.

I looked at the [code in question](https://github.com/r-lib/crayon/blob/e7f89c028f69fd92eb18fffb62ab0f1a947949f4/R/aab-num-ansi-colors.R#L91) and so in my ~/.Rprofile I added 

```
options(
  cli.num_colors=256L
)
```

This works now, but it took some digging.

For reference, `Sys.getenv("TERM")` outputs `screen-256color` or `xterm-256color`, respectively.


Ideally the "yo" would be green for the first expression too.  I think the problem might be at [this line](https://github.com/gaborcsardi/crayon/blob/master/R/machinery.r#L10) whereby you replace any prior closing tags with opening tags and move the closing tags to the end.
